full_judgment:
Daliluddin  Ahmed, J - This is an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for con-donation of delay in filing an appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act, 1974. By judgment and order, dated 23-11-85, passed by the Special Tribunal, 2nd Court, Rangpur in Special Tribunal Case No. 33 of 1984, the appellant petitioner was convicted under section 376 of the Penal Code read with section 40 of the Special Pours Act, 1974 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10 (ten) years and so pay a fine of Taka 5,000 (Five thousand) in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for two years more. The appeal was presented for filing in the office of the High Court Division, Rangpur on 20-11-1985, but as it was out of time by 28 days, the appeal was returned to the learned advocate for the appellant-petitioner. Thereafter the said appeal has been presented before this Court with an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay on the ground that the petitioner is a poor rickshaw puller and due to his pecuniary difficulties he could not file the appeal within time before this Court. 

 2. Now the question for our determination is whether the provisions of section 5 of the Limitation Act has any application to an appeal preferred under section 30 of the Special Powers Act. 

 3. Mr. Azizul Haque, the learned advocate for the appellant petitioner contended that there is no bar to the applicability of section 5 of the Limitation Act in an appeal filed under section 30 of the Special Powers Act and this Court has ample power to condone the delay if it is satisfied that there is sufficient ground for the delay. In support of his contention he has relied upon the case of Mustafa @ Mustafizur Rahman vs. The State, 1985 BLD 335. 

 4. Mr. Kaisaruddin Ahmed, the learned Deputy Attorney General who appeared for the State argued that its view of the provision of section 2 sub-section (2) clauses (a) & (b) of the Limitation Act, section 5 of the said Act has no manner of application for condoning a delay in filing an appeal under section 30 of the Special Power Act. In support of the above contention he  as relied upon the case of Syed Mahmud Alam vs. Syed Mehdi Hussain and 2 others, PLD 1970 Lahore, 6 and the case of Chheda Lal Jain vs. Officer, Commanding Station Meerui Cantonment, AIR 1941 Allahabad 207. 

 (2) Where any special law prescribes for any suit, appeal or application a period of limitation different from the period practiced thereafter by the first schedule, the provision of section 3 shall apply, as If such period were prescribed thereof in that schedule, and for the purpose of determining any period of limitation prescribed for any suit, appeal or application by any special law. 

 6. On consideration of sub-section (2) as a whole it appears that where a special law provided for limitation different from that provided by the first schedule of the Limitation Act the provisions of sections 4-9-18 and 22 of the Limitation Act shall apply for determination of limitation unless those are excluded by the special law and the remaining provisions including sub-section 5 of the Limitation Act shall not apply unless it is made applicable by the special enactment. 

 7. There is no doubt that the Special Powers Act, 1974 is a special law and the Special Powers Act provides for 30 days limitation for Mira en appeal before the High Court Division whereas Article 155 of the Limitation Act prescribes 60 days of limitation for filing an appeal to the Court. So period of limitation prescribed by the Special Powers Act is different from the period of Limitation provided in the Limitation Act. So section 3 of the Limitation Act shall apply as if section 30 of the Limitation Act has been provided in the first schedule of the Act. 

 8. The words "the remaining provisions of this Act shall not apply" appearing in clause (b) of section 29 sub-section (2) is very significant. Provisions of section 4.9.18 and 22 are applicable in special law unless these are specially excluded by the special law and other provisions including section 5 of the Limitation Act are not applicable unless those are made specifically applicable by the special law. This view finds support from a number of decisions of indo-Pakistan Sub-continent. In the case of Syed Mahmud  Alam-Versus-Syed Mehedi Hussain and 2 others, PLD 1970 Lahore 6, their Lordships of a Division Bench of the Lahore High Court, after consideration of the applicability of section 5 of the Limitation Act to an appeal under the Displaced Person (Land Settlement) Act, which is a special law observed as follows : 

 "The words ''by or under any enactment" Indicate that section 5 of the Limitation Act is not of general application to all enactments, but can be made applicable by the provisions of an enactments, This further supports the view that section 29, being a special provision dealing with local and special laws, will override the provisions of section 5 of the Limitation Act. If that is so, the date contained in clause (b) of sub-section (2) of section 29, of the Limitation Act being in absolute terms will prevail and the application of section 5  of the Limitation Act, shall have is ha held as excluded in respect of special and local laws. The Act under consideration being admittedly a special law the above discussion shows that section 5 of the Limitation Act is not applicable to appeals filed under sensation 18 of that Act". 

 9. In the case of Chheda Lal Jain Versus Officer, Commanding Station Meerat Cantonment, AIR 1941 Allahabad 207 their Lordship of a Division Bench of Allahabad High Court after consideration of section 5 and section 29 of the Limitation Act and section 29 Cantonments (House Accommodation) Act 1923, held as follows:- 

 "The Cantonments.(House Accommodation) Act is a Special Act, and section 5 of the Limitation act, is nor applicable to an appeal under section 29, Cantonments (House Accommodation) Act". 

 10. The learned Advocate for the appellant-petitioner in support of his contention that the provision of section 5 is applicable in the instant case has cited the case of Mostafa @ Mustafizur Rahman Vs The State, 1985 BLD 335, wherein his Lordship Mr. Justice Md. Altaf Hossein, J, held as follows :— Section 3 is subject to a. 5. Section 5 has not beau affected by the second part of sub. section (2) of section 29, It follows that the power of the Court to admit an appeal even after the expiry of period of limitation prescribed by the Special Law under section 5 remain." 

 11. In view of the above discussions of the relevant sections of the Limitation Act and the decisions not above, we are unable to accept the principles laid down by the single Bench of the Dhaka High our Division. 

 12. We are of the opinion that section 5 of the Limitation Act has no manner of application for condonation of delay in filing an appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers. Act 1974 and we have no jurisdiction to entertain such an application.
